You are re-extracting structured fields from a Fareharbor tour/activity's raw description text.

Field definitions:
- redo_desc_about: The general narrative that describes WHAT THE EXPERIENCE IS — the overview or "about the experience" text. Typically flowing prose introducing the activity. If the raw text has a "description:" label or an ##About header, its content goes here.
- redo_desc_highlights: Specific, concrete selling points that would make a customer choose THIS experience over others — unique features, standout moments, named attractions, distinctive elements, or award-winning aspects. If the raw text has a "highlights:" label or ##Highlights header, its content goes here. The label is the tiebreaker: labeled content ALWAYS goes to highlights even if it reads like narrative.
- redo_desc_what_included: Items, services, or amenities provided at no extra cost, even if it says "Journey Inclusions" or "Package Inclusions" or "Tour Includes".
- redo_desc_what_excluded: Items, services, or costs explicitly NOT included in the base price. Look for phrases like "at your own expense", "not included", "additional cost", "extra charge", "optional add-on at extra cost". An "Optional Add-Ons" section listing upgrades available at extra cost = what_excluded.
- redo_desc_itinerary: A time-based or step-by-step sequence of events that happen DURING the experience. Must contain time signals (e.g. "9am", "Day 1", "then", "next", "first...then...finally") OR named stops/locations visited in a specific order with clear sequence. A list of product OPTIONS or choices (e.g. Option A / Option B / Option C) is NOT an itinerary — put that in redo_desc_what_included or redo_desc_other.
- redo_desc_what_to_bring: A list of things the customer must bring or wear, even if it says "Please Bring" or appears in a "More Info" section.
- redo_desc_duration_text: How long the experience lasts, as stated in the text.
- redo_desc_requirements: Age limits, height/weight minimums, health warnings, fitness level requirements, even if buried inside a "Tour Requirements" or "Please Note" section. When content is ambiguous: if it restricts WHO can participate (age, height, weight, health, fitness) or what they MUST do or have before participating — it is requirements. If it simply describes the experience or recommends something, it belongs in redo_desc_about.
- redo_desc_cancellation: Refund rules, cancellation windows, rebooking fees, weather-cancellation policy, no-show policy.
- redo_desc_check_in: Instructions about arrival or check-in stated in the description text.
- redo_min_age: The minimum age requirement, sourced specifically from an embedded "min_age:" label when present. If no such label exists, leave "".
- redo_max_age: The maximum age requirement, sourced specifically from an embedded "max_age:" label when present. If no such label exists, leave "".
- redo_group_size: The group size limit, sourced specifically from an embedded "group_size:" label when present. If no such label exists, leave "".
- redo_meeting_point: The meeting point / starting location, sourced specifically from an embedded "meeting_point:" label when present. If no such label exists, leave "".
- redo_desc_other: This field is NARROW. It accepts ONLY these three kinds of content:
   1. Pricing, rates, rate cards, and price lists
   2. Booking, payment, and reservation instructions (how to book, payment methods, deposit terms, availability enquiries)
   3. Promotional cross-sell to the operator's OTHER products or tours (e.g. "see you next time on our Hunter Valley tour")
  Nothing else belongs here. Do NOT put general narrative, descriptive prose, supplier background, testimonials, or unclassifiable text in redo_desc_other.

CORE RULES:

1. SOURCE OF TRUTH RULE: The RAW TEXT is the only source of truth. Read it yourself and derive every field from it directly.

2. EMBEDDED LABEL RULE: The raw text often contains embedded labels in the form "label: value" — for example "highlights:", "what_to_bring:", "what_is_included:", "min_age:", "max_age:", "group_size:", "meeting_point:", "duration:", "accessibility:", "description:". When such a label appears, the content following it belongs to that labeled field. Respect the label — do NOT guess or override it with your own judgment. This is the single most important rule for correct classification.

LABEL MAPPING — when these labels appear in the raw text, the content following them goes to the field shown. This mapping is authoritative and overrides your own judgment:
  description:            -> redo_desc_about
  highlights:             -> redo_desc_highlights
  what_is_included:      -> redo_desc_what_included
  what_is_not_included:  -> redo_desc_what_excluded
  extras:                 -> redo_desc_what_excluded
  itinerary:              -> redo_desc_itinerary
  what_to_bring:          -> redo_desc_what_to_bring
  duration:               -> redo_desc_duration_text
  min_age:                -> redo_min_age
  max_age:                -> redo_max_age
  group_size:             -> redo_group_size
  meeting_point:          -> redo_meeting_point
  cancellation_summary:  -> redo_desc_cancellation
  check_in_details:      -> redo_desc_check_in
  restrictions:           -> redo_desc_requirements
  special_requirements:  -> redo_desc_requirements
  accessibility:          -> redo_desc_requirements
  disclaimers:            -> redo_desc_other
  faqs:                   -> redo_desc_other
  pricing:                -> redo_desc_other
Any label not in this list: classify its content by meaning, and if it fits nothing, put it in redo_desc_about unless it is pricing, booking/payment instructions, or promotional cross-sell, in which case it goes in redo_desc_other.

3. MARKDOWN HEADER RULE: The raw text may also contain markdown headers (## Highlights, # What's Included) or bolded headings. Treat these the same as labels — content under a header belongs to that header's field. The opening paragraph of a description is NOT highlights by default — it is general description text and belongs in the redo_desc_about field unless explicitly labeled as highlights.

HEADER MAPPING — treat these header variants as equivalent to the labels above:
  About / Tour Description / Description / Tour Summary        -> redo_desc_about
  Highlights / Tour Highlights                                  -> redo_desc_highlights
  Included / What's Included / Inclusions / Journey Inclusions /
    Package Inclusions / '<Brand> Includes:'                    -> redo_desc_what_included
  Not Included / What's Not Included / Exclusions               -> redo_desc_what_excluded
  Itinerary                                                     -> redo_desc_itinerary
  What to Bring / Bring / Dress Code / What to Wear             -> redo_desc_what_to_bring
  Duration                                                      -> redo_desc_duration_text
  Requirements / Tour Requirements / Waiver / Restrictions      -> redo_desc_requirements
  Cancellation Policy / Cancellation                            -> redo_desc_cancellation
  Rates / Prices / Pricing / Schedule / More info /
    Important Note / Important Information / FAQs /
    Who Is This Tour For? / Perfect for / At A Glance /
    Choose Your Experience                                      -> see SPLIT WITHIN SECTION RULE, then redo_desc_other for whatever remains (or redo_desc_about if the remainder is narrative, per the DEFAULT DESTINATION RULE)

4. NO CONTENT LOSS RULE: Never lose or truncate content. Extract the FULL text for each field, not a summary. Any content you cannot confidently classify into a named field goes into redo_desc_about (or redo_desc_other if it is pricing, booking instructions, or cross-sell — see DEFAULT DESTINATION RULE). Nothing from the raw text should be silently dropped.

EMPTY-WHEN-ABSENT RULE:
First determine whether the raw text is STRUCTURED or UNSTRUCTURED.
- STRUCTURED = the raw text contains at least one embedded "label:" marker OR at least one markdown/bolded section header.
- UNSTRUCTURED = the raw text contains no labels and no headers at all; it is pure flowing prose.

If the text is STRUCTURED:
  redo_desc_highlights MUST be "" unless a highlights: label or a Highlights-style header actually exists in the text.
  You MUST NOT create highlights by rewording, condensing, or bullet-pointing the description/about narrative.
  The supplier organised their content deliberately. If they did not provide highlights, the correct answer is an empty string. An empty field is CORRECT and is not a failure.

If the text is UNSTRUCTURED:
  You may classify content by meaning, including populating highlights with specific concrete selling points — but you must still copy the exact original wording (see VERBATIM RULE).

DESTINATION CLAUSE — this clause overrides nothing above but is mandatory:
Declining to place content in a field is NEVER permission to delete that content. When you leave redo_desc_highlights empty because no highlights label or header exists, the content you declined MUST still be placed somewhere:
  - Narrative or descriptive prose about the experience -> redo_desc_about
  - Sequenced or time-ordered content -> redo_desc_itinerary
  - Anything else that fits no named field -> redo_desc_other
An empty highlights field is correct. A deleted sentence is never correct. Every sentence in the raw text must appear in at least one output field.

DEFAULT DESTINATION RULE:
redo_desc_about is the DEFAULT home for any description content that does not clearly belong to a named field.
If a sentence or paragraph is narrative, descriptive, background, supplier information, a testimonial, or simply does not fit any named field — and it is NOT pricing, booking instructions, or cross-sell to other products — it goes in redo_desc_about.
Do not leave such content out, and do not put it in redo_desc_other. redo_desc_other is reserved for the three narrow categories only.
Concrete example: the raw text contains "Our first stop is at Sydney Zoo for a close-up encounter with Australia's unique fauna" and there is no highlights label in the text. This is descriptive narrative. It goes in redo_desc_about, appended after the opening paragraph. It must NOT be dropped, and it must NOT go in redo_desc_other.

NO CROSS-FIELD BORROWING RULE:
Never populate redo_desc_highlights by copying, selecting, or summarising lines from redo_desc_what_included, redo_desc_itinerary, redo_desc_about, or any other field. Highlights may ONLY be filled from content that the supplier presented as highlights — under a highlights: label, a Highlights-style header, or (on UNSTRUCTURED prose only) content that is genuinely written as a distinct list of selling points.
If no such content exists, redo_desc_highlights = "". Selecting lines from another field is not extraction and is forbidden.
Example of a VIOLATION: the raw text has a what_is_included: section listing "Sydney Zoo Admission including Roo feeding" and no highlights section. Outputting "Sydney Zoo Admission including Roo feeding" in redo_desc_highlights is forbidden — highlights must be empty and that line belongs only in redo_desc_what_included.

NO DUPLICATION RULE:
Every sentence of the raw text belongs in EXACTLY ONE output field. Extracting is MOVING text, not copying it.
When you place a sentence into a specific field, that sentence must NOT also appear in redo_desc_about or in any other field. Remove it from everywhere else.
Test yourself before answering: pick any sentence in your output and search for it in your other fields. If it appears twice, you have duplicated it -- delete every copy except the single best-fitting one.
Example of a VIOLATION: the raw text has one rates block. You put it in the correct field AND leave the same words in redo_desc_about. The portal then renders that block twice on the same page. Keep it in one field only.
This rule NEVER licenses deleting content. If a sentence fits no specific field, it stays in redo_desc_about -- once. Removing a duplicate means removing the extra copy, never the last copy.

NO INVENTION RULE:
Every word you output must already exist in the raw text. Do not add framing, transitions, headings, summaries, or connective phrases of your own.
Do not write placeholder prose such as "No content found in raw text for this field." If a field has no content, return an empty string "".
Do not restate a fact in your own words to make a field look complete. An empty field is correct and expected when the raw text does not cover it.
Test yourself: if a phrase in your output cannot be found in the raw text by searching for it, you invented it. Remove it.

VERBATIM RULE:
Copy the exact words from the raw text. Do not reword, rephrase, condense, summarise, or restructure prose into bullet-style sentences.
Test yourself: if you are about to start a sentence with a verb that does not appear in that position in the raw text, you are rewording. Stop and copy the original wording instead.
Example of a VIOLATION: raw text says "the Fragrance and Aroma's coffee welcomes us for our relaxing Morning Tea" and you output "Enjoy a relaxing morning tea at the Fragrance and Aroma's coffee café." That is rewriting, not extracting. It is forbidden.
You may strip HTML tags and markdown symbols. You may split a paragraph into lines. You may not change the words themselves.

SPLIT WITHIN SECTION RULE:
A single labeled section, header, or bulleted list may contain content belonging to several different fields. Never place a whole mixed block into one field. Split it line by line and route each line to its correct field.
Example: a section headed "At A Glance" containing:
  - 2-7 people per booking
  - Skipper to be over 20 years old
  - BYO food and drinks
  - Inc all safety equipment + boat training
must be split: "2-7 people per booking" -> redo_group_size; "Skipper to be over 20 years old" -> redo_desc_requirements; "BYO food and drinks" -> redo_desc_what_to_bring; "Inc all safety equipment + boat training" -> redo_desc_what_included. Nothing is left in other.

Extraction rules:
- Extract ONLY what is genuinely present in the raw text
- Do not invent, infer beyond what is written, or pull in outside knowledge
- If a field has no content, return ""

COMPLETENESS SELF-CHECK — perform this before you return your answer:
1. Re-read the raw text from the start.
2. For every paragraph, bullet, and sentence in it, confirm that its text appears in at least one of your output fields.
3. If any paragraph, bullet, or sentence does not appear anywhere in your output, add it now — to the field whose definition fits best (redo_desc_about by default per the DEFAULT DESTINATION RULE, or redo_desc_other only if it is pricing, booking instructions, or cross-sell).
4. Only greetings, sign-offs, and pure branding lines may be absent from your output. Everything else must be present.
Content completeness takes priority over tidy classification. It is better to place a sentence in 'about' than to lose it.

Return ONLY this JSON, no commentary:
{"redo_desc_about": "", "redo_desc_highlights": "", "redo_desc_what_included": "", "redo_desc_what_excluded": "", "redo_desc_itinerary": "", "redo_desc_what_to_bring": "", "redo_desc_duration_text": "", "redo_desc_requirements": "", "redo_desc_cancellation": "", "redo_desc_check_in": "", "redo_min_age": "", "redo_max_age": "", "redo_group_size": "", "redo_meeting_point": "", "redo_desc_other": ""}

It is NOT promotional text. It commonly uses ## markdown headers but may also use plain paragraphs or bullet lists with no headers.

Field definitions:

- redo_booking_what_not_to_bring: Items the customer is told NOT to bring or that are prohibited. This is a DIFFERENT field from what_to_bring — never merge them.
- redo_booking_inclusions: Items or services provided at no extra cost, even if under "##We Provide" or "##What is Included".
- redo_booking_location: The permanent physical address or meeting point for the activity — street address, suburb, map link, landmark description, parking information, directions to find the venue.
- redo_booking_check_in: What to DO when you arrive on the day — present your ticket, sign a waiver, go to reception, meet your guide at a specific spot, complete registration. This is about ACTIONS on arrival.
- redo_booking_departure_info: Time-based departure instructions — when to be there, what time the tour leaves, pickup window, which wharf/terminal/meeting spot the tour LEAVES from. This is about TIMING and DEPARTURE LOCATION.
  Key rule distinguishing location vs departure_info: an address alone -> location. A time alone -> departure_info. Both together -> split them into their respective fields.
  Key rule distinguishing check_in vs departure_info: if content has both timing/location and arrival actions — split it: timing/location -> departure_info, arrival actions -> check_in.
- redo_booking_itinerary: A time-based or step-by-step sequence of events that happen DURING the experience. Must contain time signals (e.g. "9am", "Day 1", "then", "next", "first...then...finally") OR named stops/locations visited in a specific order with clear sequence. A list of product OPTIONS or choices (e.g. Option A / Option B / Option C) is NOT an itinerary — put that in redo_booking_other.
- redo_booking_important_info: Health warnings, age limits, fitness requirements, safety rules, waivers.
- redo_booking_cancellation: Refund rules, cancellation windows, weather policy.
- redo_booking_faqs: Question-and-answer content, however formatted (numbered Q&A, "##FAQs", "##Frequently asked questions"). Capture the FULL question and answer text for every FAQ, not a selection.
- redo_booking_before_arrival: Actions the customer must complete BEFORE the day of the activity — registrations, form completion, licence applications, pre-study, online course enrolment, numbered preparation steps. Distinct from check_in, which is actions ON arrival.
- redo_booking_contact: ALL operator contact information and communication instructions — phone numbers, email addresses, website URLs, document and form links, and instructions about how to communicate (e.g. "do not reply to this email, email us at X", "call Paul on X", "fill in this form and send it back").
- redo_booking_other: Anything that does not fit above. Never lose content — if you cannot classify it, put it in other. Promotional discount codes and multi-tour promotional content (e.g. "book 2 tours and save 10%", cross-sell mentions of other tours, referral codes) that operators embed inside booking notes ARE genuinely useful operational content and MUST be captured in redo_booking_other rather than excluded as filler.

    Registration / How to access ... / numbered prep steps      -> redo_booking_before_arrival
  Cancellation / Refund policy                                  -> redo_booking_cancellation

- redo_desc_highlights: Specific, concrete selling points that would make a customer choose THIS experience over others — unique features, standout moments, named attractions, distinctive elements, or award-winning aspects. If the raw text has a "highlights:" label or ##Highlights header, its content goes here. The label is the tiebreaker: labeled content ALWAYS goes to highlights even if it reads like narrative.
- redo_desc_what_included: Items, services, or amenities provided at no extra cost, even if it says "Journey Inclusions" or "Package Inclusions" or "Tour Includes".
- redo_desc_what_excluded: Items, services, or costs explicitly NOT included in the base price. Look for phrases like "at your own expense", "not included", "additional cost", "extra charge", "optional add-on at extra cost". An "Optional Add-Ons" section listing upgrades available at extra cost = what_excluded.
- redo_desc_itinerary: A time-based or step-by-step sequence of events that happen DURING the experience. Must contain time signals (e.g. "9am", "Day 1", "then", "next", "first...then...finally") OR named stops/locations visited in a specific order with clear sequence. A list of product OPTIONS or choices (e.g. Option A / Option B / Option C) is NOT an itinerary — put that in redo_desc_what_included or redo_desc_other.
- redo_desc_what_to_bring: A list of things the customer must bring or wear, even if it says "Please Bring" or appears in a "More Info" section.
- redo_desc_duration_text: How long the experience lasts, as stated in the text.
- redo_desc_requirements: Age limits, height/weight minimums, health warnings, fitness level requirements, even if buried inside a "Tour Requirements" or "Please Note" section. When content is ambiguous: if it restricts WHO can participate (age, height, weight, health, fitness) or what they MUST do or have before participating — it is requirements. If it simply describes the experience or recommends something, it belongs in redo_desc_about.
- redo_desc_cancellation: Refund rules, cancellation windows, rebooking fees, weather-cancellation policy, no-show policy.
- redo_desc_check_in: Instructions about arrival or check-in stated in the description text.
- redo_min_age: The minimum age requirement, sourced specifically from an embedded "min_age:" label when present. If no such label exists, leave "".
- redo_max_age: The maximum age requirement, sourced specifically from an embedded "max_age:" label when present. If no such label exists, leave "".
- redo_group_size: The group size limit, sourced specifically from an embedded "group_size:" label when present. If no such label exists, leave "".
- redo_meeting_point: The meeting point / starting location, sourced specifically from an embedded "meeting_point:" label when present. If no such label exists, leave "".
